_comment: Every third-party dependency MEGATRON links, with the licence it was
approved under. ci/policy_check.py (LICENCE) fails the build on any
dependency in a build file that is not listed here.
WHY AN ALLOWLIST AND NOT A LICENCE-SCANNING SERVICE:
the policy gate is stdlib-only and offline by design, so that it runs
identically on a laptop and a runner and can never itself become a
supply-chain concern in a project whose entire pitch is not being
MagnusBilling. A network call to resolve a licence is a network call that
can be wrong, slow, or absent -- and a gate that silently degrades when
The cost is that adding a dependency requires a human to write a line
here. That is the intended cost. MEGATRON is proprietary and
distributed to licensees, so a GPL/AGPL/LGPL dependency is not a licence
problem to be discovered later -- it is a product that cannot ship.
Adding an entry means asserting you checked the licence of THAT VERSION.

org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib.why: The language runtime. Unavoidable, and Apache-2.0 throughout.

org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-test.why: Test only. Never linked into a shipped binary.

org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launch.why: Test only, never distributed. EPL-2.0 is a weak copyleft that reaches only the EPL'd files themselves, and this is a test-runtime dependency that is not linked into any shipped artifact.

org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-serializat.why: JSON on the provisioning API. Compile-time code generation rather than runtime reflection, which matters on a service the authorizer sits next to.

io.ktor:ktor-server-core.why: HTTP server for the provisioning API. Chosen over Spring Boot for this service because it starts in milliseconds and carries no reflective classpath scanning -- the smaller the running surface on a box that also terminates SIP, the better.

io.ktor:ktor-server-netty.why: Ktor's Netty engine. Netty itself is Apache-2.0.

io.ktor:ktor-server-content-negotiation.why: Binds JSON to the routes. Also how the API is kept JSON-only: MagnusBilling's CVE-2025-2609/2610 were APIs served as text/html.

io.ktor:ktor-server-status-pages.why: Turns exceptions into RFC 9457 problem documents instead of leaking a stack trace to a caller.

io.ktor:ktor-server-auth.why: Bearer authentication, and the operator/customer scope split the contract requires.

io.ktor:ktor-server-call-logging.why: Request logging. Needed to answer 'who moved this balance' at all.

io.ktor:ktor-server-test-host.why: Test only. Runs the real routes in-process so the API is tested as an API rather than as a pile of functions.

io.ktor:ktor-client-content-negotiation.why: Test only. The test client's JSON support.

org.slf4j:slf4j-simple.why: SLF4J binding, required because Ktor logs through SLF4J. Chosen over Logback deliberately -- see the note below.

org.slf4j:slf4j-api.why: The logging facade Ktor is written against.

org.xerial:sqlite-jdbc.why: Durable storage for a single node, and the only database that can be TESTED on the machine this is being written on. The SQL is deliberately portable so the PostgreSQL store is a schema file and a JDBC URL rather than a rewrite -- see docs/STORAGE.md.

carrying, documenting, and defending in every licensing conversation with
an operator we sell to, for a logging backend.
